title: Cell-ELONA
author: Guillermo Fernández Rodríguez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7umhnu6

steps.title: Inoculate E. coli culture
steps.instruction: Pick a single colony of E. coli DH5α from an LB agar plate with a sterile pipette tip and inoculate it into 10 mL LB broth; incubate the liquid culture overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: First centrifugation and resuspension
steps.instruction: Spin the overnight culture at 4000 rpm for 5 min, discard the supernatant, collect the pellet and resuspend it in 10 mL of 50 mM NaHCO₃‑Na₂CO₃ buffer, pH 9.6; mix by inverting the tube.

steps.title: Second centrifugation and resuspension
steps.instruction: Spin the suspension again at 4000 rpm for 5 min, discard the supernatant, collect the pellet and resuspend it in 8 mL of 50 mM NaHCO₃‑Na₂CO₃ buffer, pH 9.6; mix by inverting the tube.

steps.title: Adjust optical density to 1
steps.instruction: Measure the absorbance of the suspension at 600 nm; if necessary, dilute the sample with 50 mM NaHCO₃‑Na₂CO₃, pH 9.6, until the absorbance reaches 1.0.

steps.title: Dilute sample 1:4
steps.instruction: Transfer the adjusted suspension to an Eppendorf tube and dilute it 1:4 with 50 mM NaHCO₃‑Na₂CO₃, pH 9.6.

steps.title: Plate bacterial sample and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of the diluted bacterial suspension to each well of a Nunc MaxiSorp 96‑well plate; add coating buffer to designated negative‑control wells. Incubate the plate overnight at 4 °C with agitation at 260 rpm.

steps.title: Remove coating buffer
steps.instruction: Carefully aspirate the coating buffer from all wells without touching the well surface or disturbing the attached bacteria.

steps.title: Wash plate with PBS‑Tween
steps.instruction: Wash the plate three times by adding 200 µL of PBS 1× containing 0.1 % Tween to each well, then aspirate; after the third wash, remove any remaining drops.

steps.title: Block plate with BSA
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of PBS 1× with 5 % BSA to each well and incubate for 1 hour (01:00:00) at 260 rpm.

steps.title: Prepare digoxigenin aptamers
steps.instruction: Denature digoxigenin‑labelled aptamers by heating at 95 °C for 10 min, then cool on ice for 10 min; aptamers should already be prepared at the required concentrations.

steps.title: Wash plate post‑aptamer prep
steps.instruction: Wash the plate three times with 200 µL PBS 1× 0.1 % Tween, aspirating after each wash; discard the final drops.

steps.title: Add structured aptamers and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of the structured aptamer solution to each well and incubate for 1 hour (01:00:00).

steps.title: Wash plate after aptamer binding
steps.instruction: Wash the plate three times with 200 µL PBS 1× 0.1 % Tween, aspirating after each wash.

steps.title: Add anti‑digoxigenin antibody
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1:1000 dilution of anti‑digoxigenin antibody in Aptamer buffer containing 0.2 % BSA; add 100 µL of this diluted antibody to each well and incubate at room temperature for 1 hour (01:00:00).

steps.title: Wash plate after antibody
steps.instruction: Wash the plate three times with 200 µL PBS 1× 0.1 % Tween, aspirating after each wash.

steps.title: Add ABTS substrate and read absorbance
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of ABTS solution to each well; measure absorbance at 405 nm every 10 min for a total of 1 hour.
